value: The Tenancy Law of Lagos State 2011 governs tenancies of premises in Lagos State; other Nigerian states have their own laws.
source_publisher: Lagos State Ministry of Justice (Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011)
note: Lagos State only. Tenancy Law of Lagos State 2011, as published in the Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011 on the Ministry of Justice site (English). Later amendments and the tenancy laws of Nigeria's other states were not checked.

value: A landlord may not demand or receive from a sitting tenant more than six months' rent from a monthly tenant or one year's rent from a yearly tenant, and from a new or prospective tenant not more than one year's rent; paying or receiving more is an offence with a fine of N100,000 or three months' imprisonment (s. 4).
source_publisher: Lagos State Ministry of Justice (Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011)
note: Lagos State only. Tenancy Law of Lagos State 2011, as published in the Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011 on the Ministry of Justice site (English). Later amendments and the tenancy laws of Nigeria's other states were not checked.

value: On every rent payment the landlord must issue a receipt stating the date, the names and addresses of landlord and tenant, the premises, the amount and the period covered; failure is punishable by a fine of N100,000 (s. 5).
source_publisher: Lagos State Ministry of Justice (Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011)
note: Lagos State only. Tenancy Law of Lagos State 2011, as published in the Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011 on the Ministry of Justice site (English). Later amendments and the tenancy laws of Nigeria's other states were not checked.

field: Lagos State: notice to end a tenancy
value: Where the agreement sets no notice, the notice to end a tenancy is one week for a tenant at will, one month for a monthly tenant, three months for a quarterly or half-yearly tenant and six months for a yearly tenant (s. 13(1)).
source_publisher: Lagos State Ministry of Justice (Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011)
note: Lagos State only. Tenancy Law of Lagos State 2011, as published in the Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011 on the Ministry of Justice site (English). Later amendments and the tenancy laws of Nigeria's other states were not checked.

value: A monthly tenancy lapses where the tenant is six months in arrears, and a quarterly or half-yearly tenancy where the tenant is one year in arrears, and the court makes an order for possession and arrears (s. 13(2)-(3)).
source_publisher: Lagos State Ministry of Justice (Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011)
note: Lagos State only. Tenancy Law of Lagos State 2011, as published in the Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011 on the Ministry of Justice site (English). Later amendments and the tenancy laws of Nigeria's other states were not checked.

field: Lagos State: end of fixed term
value: After a fixed term ends by passage of time no notice to quit is needed, but a landlord who goes to court to recover possession must first serve seven days' written notice of intention (Form TL5) (s. 13(5)).
source_publisher: Lagos State Ministry of Justice (Lagos State Official Gazette No. 37 of 26 August 2011)
